name: Local Maximal-Cube Traces Cover Every Cornerless Cube
statement: Let $C$ be a maximal cube of a nonempty cube family $X$, and let $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ be the other maximal cubes meeting it. The corners of $X$ lying in $C$ are exactly $C\setminus\bigcup_i(C\cap C_i)$. Moreover $C_i$ meets $C_j$ exactly when their traces on $C$ meet. Thus in a cornerless family the nonempty proper traces $C\cap C_i$ cover $C$, their intersection graph is the neighbour graph of $C$, and deleting repetitions and redundant traces gives an irredundant proper-subcube cover.
proof: A vertex of $C$ fails to be a corner exactly when another maximal cube contains it, proving the complement formula. If two neighbouring cubes meet each other, the three pairwise-intersecting hypercube subcubes $C,C_i,C_j$ have common intersection by Helly; the reverse implication is immediate. Cornerlessness makes the traces cover, and an inclusion-minimal covering subfamily is irredundant.
